Made by D.S. Mischenko Forwarded by D.S.I. O Atkinson
(批：P.a & D.C (4) Information C 39 P.A. to D.C. (Sp. Br.))
(印：DEPUTY COMMISSIONER 30 NOV. 1939 (CRIM. DIV.))
(批：FILE C/)
Mrs. K.V.SIMONOVA, the licensee of Houses No.91-97, Fearon Road, came to this office on November 28, 1939, and informed the undersigned of her intention to cancel the lodging house licence in respect of above premises. She stated that the houses are actually owned and operated by a Mrs. V. Gorskaya with whom she severed all connections.
Mrs. Varvara or Vera Gorskaya, naturalized Japanese subject of Russian origin, who is better known under the name of Viola Smith, C.R.O. F-1096, is a well known brothel keeper in Shanghai. She is at present operating brothels at 650 Wei Hai Wei Road, 50-52 Love Lane, 97 Fearon Road, and it is believed that another establishment numbering some 30 Korean girls, also owned by her, is operating on Boone Road, and is patronized mainly by the Japanese Military.
Following the outbreak of the Sino-Japanese Hostilities locally, Mrs. V. Gorskaya started a transport company and is reported to own about 30 motor-trucks which do business in the Japanese occupied areas. It is also reported that Mrs. V. Gorskaya is engaged in an import and export business and for this purpose she has an office in the Liza Hardoon Building, Nanking Road; the firm being known as the "Oriental Trans-Pacific Syndicates".
There is no definite proof as to the present national status of Mrs. V. Gorskaya available, but it should be mentioned that the records at the Finger Print Bureau show that on 18-4-35, she was charged at the 1st Shanghai Special District Court with keeping open a brothel and sentenced to 10 days detention.

Subject Notes On Foreign Criminals And Suspects.
Made by and Forwarded by D.S.I. Golder.

The attached which comprises notes on Foreign
Criminals and Suspects has been prepared in accordance with
the instructions of the Acting Commissioner dated November 5,
1935.

In comparison with the information contained in
the notes forwarded by the Straits Settlement Police, the
attached show in many instances a lack of essential detail,
due to the fact that the preparation of these notes is an
innovation.

comprise information on approximately 100 persons and include
reference to some 450. To produce a work of informative
value it will be necessary to prepare notes on some 500 persons,
with reference, if the aforementioned ratio is maintained, to
some 2,000. This would entail about 15 months work at the
present rate of preparation.

ABOLNIK, Samuil N., Russian, born at Vilno in 1905
C.R.O.F-746. Files: D.2237, D.6202, C.5353, C.989/32,
I.O. 8646, D.I.S. 1067/33.
Associates:
Pochkovsky. Soolevitch, M. Soolevitch, I.
Beilin, J. Shapoonoff, E.L. Polonetzky.

Following the German occupation of Vilno in 1917
Abolnik and his brother fled to America where they remained for
three months. Samuil went to Harbin and was next heard of in
Tientsin in 1923. Later in the same year he came to Shanghai
and obtained employment with the Commercial Express & Storage Co.
He subsequently worked with various transportation companies until
1930, when he made a trip to Soviet Russia. He first came to
notice locally as the result of his connection with certain
undesirable political intrigue. In November 1931 he was arrested
together with J. Beilin and charged with fraud, but the prosecution
failed. He was again arrested in July 1932 and charged with a
similar offence and sentenced to 10 months imprisonment. He
appealed and the sentence was set aside on January 25, 1933. .
Modus Operandi
Acting as a customs-broker he makes a practice of so
falsifying the accounts of importers whose business he is entrusted
with that they are charged more than the legitimate customs dues.
Last known address: 5. Yang Terrace.

Barling left the Shanghai Defence Force on November 27,

January 7, 1936, when he was fined $5.00 for failing to register
himself as a British subject.

suspected of minor pilfering and false pretences in cases where
the injured parties declined to institute proceedings against him.

Beaumont arrived in Shanghai on June 14, 1929 from

on December 5, 1925, and again escaped punishment for similar offence
on November 5, 1927.

Her third prosecution before the Shanghai 1st Special
District Court on a charge of trafficking in women was equally
unsuccessful.

Last known address: 2/08 Route Vallon, French Concession.

CATARAU, Julian, alias Kataran, alias Cataran, Roumanian
Files: I.O. 5202. I.O. 5601. I.O. 5740.
C.I.D. 9522/24. C.I.D. 8871/24.

Stamboul H.

There appears to be no report to hand covering the
arrival here of Catarau, Julian; it is known, however, that
prior to 1919 he was an anarchist and swindler. He left
Shanghai on October 25, 1919 by the s.s. Yamata Maru for Europe
and was next heard of in 1920 at Nice where he was convicted of
having stolen a large quantity of jewellery from a low class
woman and sentenced to 10 months imprisonment. He returned
to Shanghai in June 1923 and was seen on a number of occasions
in the company of one Dr. Kindler.

There is every indication that Catarau was in 1924
very anxious to keep on the right side of the Police; to effect
this he handed over various bits of information. In April
1924 he made a statement to the Police regarding the smuggling
of arms and it is believed brought about the arrest on April 6,
1924 of a German named Schilling, who at that time manager of
Frederick's Hotel. Catarau handed to the Police what he avowed
to be the plans for wholesale smuggling of arms by a large group,

(20)

operating between Peking and Shanghai and claimed that the
various consignments on arrival here were landed with the
connivance of Customs officers.
On July 28, 1924, Catarau was arrested by the River
Police in the company of A. Caban or Adriano Corban who was found
in possession of a pistol and ammunition which he had just removed
from the Italian ship "Rosandia". Catarau was handed over to
the City Police and charged but was released "not guilty" and
immediately admitted to the General Hospital suffering from acute
appendicitis.
On September 26, 1918 he was arrested by the French
Consul (Shanghai) on a charge of espionage, but was later released.
On September 28, 1923 he was brought before the Mixed
Court on a charge of assault and battery. The case against him
was however dismissed.
Last known address:

CAMPANI, Otello (or Mario), alias Sangez, Italian, born in 1912
C.R.O. F-457. Files: C. (Misc.) 107/34. D.6616. E.163/55.

Campani left the Italian Navy and took up residence in
Shanghai at the end of 1933.
In January 1934, whilst he was cohabiting with a
Japanese female named Chiyoko Tanaka alias Yoshimura, he was found
to have an unlicensed pistol and ammunition. This was duly
confiscated by the Italian Consul-General.
During September 1934 Campani became manager of the
Marseillais Bar on Broadway. The embezzlement of a substantial
sum of his employer's money coupled with his inability to keep his
fingers out of the petty cash cost him his job. At the Italian
Consular Court on January 4, 1935, he was found not guilty on the
charge of embezzlement, but was sentenced to two months

(21)

imprisonment and fined 300 Liras and costs on the count of
larceny, the sentence being suspended for two months.
During February 1935 a person masquerading under the
name of Sangez, who was believed to have been identical with
WILLIAM JOHN NOON, JAPANESE EUROPEAN
Campani, defrauded Anthony Rengel, Portuguese, of $25 by selling
him tickets for
/a bogus indecent cinema show.
Last known address: 9 Tsongchow Road.

CHAVEZ, Juan, Brazilian
Files: A.3704. C.I.D.2131.
On April 15, 1915, the gambling at Mount Pleasant, No.24
North Honan Road, was recommenced; on the door was a plate bearing
the name of J. Chavez. The place was watched for three months
by the Police but very little was found out about Chavez.
On March 26, 1926, a raid was carried out by the Police
at No.61 Bubuling Well Road and Chavez among others was taken
into custody. His person was searched and the result proved
beyond doubt that he was the operator of the establishment.
He was released on bail and brought before the Brazilian
Assessor, but the outcome of the case is not known.

He was employed as sports editor of the Shanghai Times

May 1931. He then associated himself with S.P. Balanovsky in

In January 1933 he claimed Chilean protection and became
the secretary of the now defunct Club Chileno, 837 Bubbling Well

connected with other gaming houses.
After the Club Chileno closed, Cheney again registered
himself at the American Consulate-General.

Christie served in the Navy as a warrant officer and
obtained his discharge in Hongkong in 1905, when he became a
professional boxing tutor and opened a gymnasium. The venture
was a financial failure and he was declared a bankrupt in 1906.
He absconded from Hongkong in 1907 after misappropriating a
quantity of jewellery for which offence a warrant was issued for
his arrest. He went to the F.M.S. in 1907 where he remained
until 1914, as a bookmaker. Whilst in the F.M.S. he came under
Police notice on account of the activities of his mistress a
Russian woman named "Trixie" alias Mrs. Campbell who was suspected
of espionage. At the outbreak of war, Christie joined His
Majesty's forces, serving with distinction. He rose to command a
battalion of the Scottish Rifles, being awarded the D.S.O., and
O.B.E. (military). After the war Christie returned to the F.M.S.
but proceeded to Shanghai in 1923. In Shanghai he attempted to
deal in arms on a large scale, firstly for Sun Yat Sen and later
on behalf of Chang Tso Lin, the Manchurian War Lord. During
the negotiations, he succeeded in defrauding a credulous Chinese
of a large sum of money, and left for the interior of China.
He later travelled through Japan, Java and Singapore, leaving
behind a trail of dishonoured cheques. He returned later to
Shanghai and in 1925 was convicted before His Majesty's Consular
Court on a charge of entering into negotiations for the sale of
arms and ammunition contrary to the Order-in-Council. He was
sentenced to 3 months' H.L. additional to a fine of $200. After
release from jail he went to Hongkong where on November 16, 1927,
he was convicted on a charge of obtaining money by false pretences
and sentenced to four months' H.L. An accomplice named C.
Bluhm, a Latvian, was at the same time sentenced to three months'
H.L. After release he came back to Shanghai and lived by his
wits. On February 16, 1933, at Shanghai he was convicted on
three charges of larceny and sentenced to seven months' imprisonment

(24)

on each charge concurrently. On completion of his sentence he
was banished from China to England, sailing from Shanghai on October
10, 1933. He is now in Europe and in April 1935, successfully
passed off a number of worthless cheques at Antwerp, Belgium.

COHEN, Joseph, Greek (Russian by birth), born in 1872
C.R.O. 51. Files: S.145/31. E.1168.

Associates:

Cohen is a shoplifter and a pick-pocket. In December

CORTES, Arthur, alias Arthur Phillips, alias Arika Kawashima,
claims to be Chilean, born in 1908 of a British father and Japanese
mother. Height about 5'11", slim build, pale face, clean shaven,
dark hair, married to a Eurasian of American extraction nee Minford
File : G.F. 55/28.

Cortes is a recognized Japanese subject, having come under
the notice of the local Japanese Consular Authorities some years ago
in connection with military conscription. However, he now claims
Chilean citizenship and, according to reliable information, paid a
large sum of money in order to secure the protection of the Chilean
Authorities.

Cortes was educated in Shanghai under the name of Arthur
Phillips. English is the only language he speaks. A
stenographer by profession, he has been employed with such firms as:
F. Heath & Co., 31 Peking Road, Tobacco Products Corporation, 200
Yulin Road, Hugo Reiss & Co., 15 Museum Road, and the Shanghai
Waterworks Co. Ltd., 484 Kiangse Road. He has been unemployed
for about four years and consequently has been in straitened

(25)
circumstances and is in the habit of moving about from place
to place in order to evade his creditors.
In December 1932 Cortes was connected with a gambling
den known as the "Pacific Club", No.56A Hart Road. He was
the tenant of the house and in filling up the Municipal
Registration form signed himself as the "Director" of the Club.
On January 7, 1933 Cortes called on the Deputy Commissioner
(Crime) and complained about the Police Party functioning outside
the Club, stating that the presence of the Police was causing
embarrassment to the members. However, the "Pacific Club"
closed down in April 1933 owing, it is said, to financial losses
sustained by the promoters.

CRANK, Thomas Reginald, alias Ch. S.Maitland, British
(Eurasian), born in 1888, Passport No.10500 issued by
H.B.M. Consul-General, Shanghai, 31.1.34.
C.R.C. 32. Files: D.6183. Central Registry 8274.
On June 2, 1908 at H.B.M. Consular Court, Shanghai,
on a charge of larceny, Crank was released under First Offenders
Act, being bound over to keep the peace for 12 months.
On November 15, 1909 at H.B.M. Consular Court on a charge
of obtaining money by False Pretences, he was sentenced to one
month's H. L.; on January 28, 1910 at H.B.M. Consular Court on
a charge of forgery, to 4 months H. L.; on November 1, 1914
at H.B.M. Consular Court on a charge of fraud and forgery, to
one year on each count, both sentences to run concurrently;
on August 6, 1917 at the Mixed Court on a charge of fraud (9
counts), to 7 years imprisonment (released after serving three
years).
On March 2, 1921 at the Mixed Court on a charge of fraud,
the case was dismissed on payment of $1,000.
After his fourth conviction he was struck off the
register and not recognized as a British subject.
On September 17, 1923, through the influence of
friends he was again registered as a British subject.

(26)

In 1933/34 Crank became connected with the Oriental
Construction Company and undertook large contracts in Tientsin.
Last known address: 920 North Szechuen Road.

CRAWLEY, Paul S., American
Files: B. 1219. B. 1353. E. 528. 3727.
8279. 9522. 9824. 10212.

Associates:
Bozello, S. Cartarau, J. Crawley, K.M.
Litsaridi, N. Tessier, A.H. Widler, E.

In 1927 Widler, Elly and Crawley, Knight M. (brother of
Paul S) perpetrated a swindle in arms amounting to $73,000 on an
agent of General Yang Sun, Tuchun of Szechuen Province. The
introduction was effected by A.H. Tessier who at that time was
representative of the Yangtsze Rapid Co. Inc. at Chungking.
Crawley left town soon after the final payment was made and took
with him the nine year old son of his brother Paul S. who claimed
that the boy had been kidnapped, a story that should not be given
credence as Paul S. is strongly suspected of complicity in the
swindle and not only knew but arranged that Knight should take the
boy, in case, he, Paul S, should be arrested. The case against
Widler and K.M. Crawley never came to Court.

Paul S. Crawley was again heard of on Wednesday, February
20, 1929, when he advertised in the China Press that he had roulette
wheels for sale.

During the foregoing incidents Paul S. was operating the
Velvet Ice Cream Co. at No.101 Szechuen Road and residing at various
addresses in the Settlement and the French Concession.

In 1932 he was apprehended by the American Authorities on
a charge of smuggling opium into the U.S.A. and sentenced to two
years imprisonment on McNeil Island.

In 1934 he returned to Shanghai as a passenger on the s.s.
Shanghai Maru but was refused permission to land as he had no valid
passport. He was detained on a River Police hulk and eventually
deported after transferring his business interests to Elly Widler
and Harrington of Franklin & Harrington, legal practitioners.

(27)

DEL VALLE FIGUEROA, Mexican, age 40 in 1934, Export Merchant
C.R.C. 1369. Files: G.F.55/23. D.281. D.346. B.1666.
C.R. A.9398.

Associates:
Alvarez. Fournier. Garcia.
Lefuente (or Santos.
La Fuente).

F. Del Valle arrived in Shanghai from Los Angeles in
August 1928. Nothing is known of his antecedents. On
October 17, 1928 he signed an antedated lease (the date being
31.7.28) for 151C Bubbling Well Road, which premises were owned
by La Fuente, a very intimate friend of the notorious gambler
Carlos Garcia. These premises were also leased to C. Garcia on
July 31, 1928.

No.151C Bubbling Well Road was well known as a gambling
house conducted by an employee of Garcia, one Alvarez. The
place was raided on April 2, 1928. Alvarez was arrested, tried in
the Mexican Consular Court, found guilty and fined 500 Pesos.

Undoubtedly the newly arrived Del Valle was the successor
of Alvarez, also only an employee and a scapegoat for the real owner
Garcia. F. Del Valle lived on the premises, and had his name
plate on the door, but Garcia paid the bills for two telephones,
supply of electricity and the supply of a large quantity of wines,
cigars, cigarettes and eatables. Gambling was conducted on a
large scale, three wheels being operated, about 100 or more persons
being generally present.

On May 26, 1929 the Police raided 151C Bubbling Well Road
and found about 200 gamblers on the premises. F. Del Valle met
the Police and informed them that he was the owner of the place.
The whole gambling paraphernalia, wheels, chips, etc. were seized.

As a Mexican citizen F. Del Valle appeared before the
Mexican Consul on June 22 and was released on bail. Subsequent
successful application by the Police Advocate resulted in the Consul
refusing him jurisdiction. On June 27, F. Del Valle was again
arrested and taken before the Provisional Court with Garcia, Santos
and Fournier. Bail being refused, the defendants were held in
custody. During the whole process F. Del Valle maintained his

(28)

statement that he was the owner and that Garcia only visited the
place occasionally. F. Del Valle was prepared to bear the whole
brunt of the charge in order to allow Garcia to evade punishment,
undoubtedly for a consideration.

On July 5, 1929 F. Del Valle was found guilty and sentenced
to one year's imprisonment and fined $2,000.
Last known address: 404 Yu Yuen Road.

DEMENTZEFF (or DEMENTSEFF or DEMINTZEFF or DIOMENTSEFF), Herman P.
(or Yerman G.P.), Russian, born in 1902.
C.R.C. 2007. Files: C.(Misc.)217/34. C.324/34. C.(Misc.)109/35.
E. 582. French Police.

Associates:
Sponopoulos, P.E., alias Vasiliev, P.E.

Dementzeff came to Shanghai from Harbin in 1931, having
left Harbin, it is believed, after perpetrating a fraud.

On February 31, 1932 at the Shanghai Second Special
District Court, Dementzeff was sentenced to 30 days imprisonment,
suspended for two years, for causing bodily harm.

On May 6, 1934 he was apprehended by the Shanghai Public
Safety Bureau for being in possession of two pistols and a quantity
of ammunition. In August of that year, he was unconfirmedly
reported to have turned his attention to trading in narcotics, and
is said to have endeavoured to negotiate the purchase of a large
quantity of heroin for which he intended to pass a bundle of
worthless currency notes.

Later in 1934, Dementzeff in association with P.E.
Sponopoulos, opened up a shady concern known as the International
Supply Corporation, 149 Yuen Ming Yuen Road. They subsequently
caused goods to be delivered against post-dated cheques bearing
their joint signatures which subsequently led to their appearance
in the Shanghai Second Special District Court for fraud.
Dementzeff was sentenced on November 14, 1934 to a fine of $40 or
20 days imprisonment. Sponopoulos was fined $120 or 60 days
imprisonment. The latter was summoned to appear at the First
Shanghai Special District Court in connection with the issue of

(29)

a worthless cheque by these two persons, for which he was sentenced
on March 23, 1935 to pay a fine of $20 or 10 days detention.
Last known address: 256/3 Avenue Dubail, French Concession.

DOLAN (or DOYLAN), James Stephan, American, born in Boston,
Massachusetts, U.S.A., in 1888.
Files: D.4806. B.256. B.458.

Associates:
Barton, Fred, alias Kottermeier. Felgate, R.H.
Gmehling, G. Sinclair, Betty.
Widler, Elly.

(30)

Dolan arrived in Shanghai in 1916 and was employed for a
a number of years with the China-Java Export Company, a somewhat
shady concern reported to be engaged in the smuggling of drugs and
arms into Yunnan and the Western Provinces. This firm went out
of business about 1925.

In 1925 Dolan left Shanghai for the United States. He
was next heard of in June 1926, when he was arrested in Hamburg,
Germany, in connection with the seizure of 457 tins of morphia
concealed in a cargo of tombstones consigned to Messrs Marshall
& Co., Shanghai. Dolan admitted that he endeavoured to smuggle
the drug to Shanghai, and at the Hamburg District Court on June 23,
1926, was fined 5,000 Reich Marks and costs. An American woman
named Betty Sinclair, who was living with Dolan at the time of his
arrest, was also detained by the Police but was later released.

Dolan resided in Paris for the next two or three years
and very little is known regarding his subsequent movements and
activities until April 5, 1933, when he arrived in Shanghai from the
U.S.A. He is known to have been accompanied by Fred Barton,
suspected drug smuggler, and to have brought with him a cargo of
eighty coffins which had been shipped by the National Casket Co.,
Boston, U.S.A. On arrival here, he resided with Elly Widler,
notorious arms smuggler. Shortly afterwards Dolan associated
himself with the Shanghai Casket Co. and later with the Universal
Funeral Co., located at 999 Bubbling Well Road and at 41 Moulmien
Road, respectively. The lease of these premises was terminated
and judgment was
by the landlords in June 1935, subsequently given against Dolan
in the American Court for recovery of $2,625 representing unpaid
rent.

DROOS, Naum (Norman) Mikhailvitch, Russian, born in 1897, Broker

On July 21, 1933 at the Shanghai First Special District

1.—AGOSTINI, PIERRE.
French subject, born in Indo-China in 1906. Very undesirable character with previous conviction at Saigon. Has been mixed up in very shady business transactions and leaves a trail of unpaid bills wherever he goes. Arrived in Hong Kong from Shanghai by the s.s. "Katori Maru" on 23rd December, 1932 and was met by Police to whom he stated that he was en route to Canton to try and get some information concerning one HARRY GOLDENBERG, his former partner (and for whose arrest warrant has been issued in Hong Kong). He left again for Shanghai by s.s. "Conte Verde" on 1st January, 1933. French Consul in Hong Kong has expressed the opinion that the passport on which AGOSTINI travels is no longer valid.

2.✓AKSMAN-GLOTZ, JOHN. (Paras. 42, 52 and 59 of 1934).
Born in 1893 in Rumania, served with the Rumanian Army during the war as a field officer and was a prisoner of war in Russia until 1920. He then proceeded to Shanghai where he was employed as an assistant manager. Married with four children. He arrived in Singapore from Shanghai on 16th June, 1925 and entered the employ of Raffles Hotel as an assistant manager. In 1927 he proceeded to India and later to Ceylon where he issued several worthless cheques. Warrants were issued against him and he absconded to Singapore arriving here in 1930. On 8th October, 1930, he was convicted in Singapore and fined $200 for breaches of the Aliens Ordinance.
On 12th June, 1931, he was sentenced to one month's R.I. after conviction on a charge of criminal breach of trust, also in Singapore. On 4th April, 1932, he was sentenced to one year's R.I. in Singapore after conviction on several charges of cheating. He was released from jail on 22nd February, 1933, and left for Hong Kong per s.s. "Kulmerland". On 19th March, 1934, he was ordered to be deported from the Colony by the Hong Kong Police and left for Canton on 21st March, 1934. His wife

(2)
is an inmate of the General Hospital, Singapore and his four
children having been a charge on a local charitable insti-
tution for some time.
He is a clever scoundrel who should not be permitted
to re-enter Malaya. He professes to have a considerable
knowledge of undesirable political intrigue but this is
merely a ruse adopted by him to endeavour to keep on the
right side of the authorities.
The latest report concerning this man is that he left
Yunnan Fu on horseback in July 1934 travelling in a westerly
direction without paying his hotel bill of $630. The Govern-
ment of Burma has been notified of his movements.
He arrived in Katho, Upper Burma in September 1934 hav-
ing travelled overland from Yunnanfu. He was accompanied
by M. Sokoloff, a Letvian, who was in possession of a pass-
port No. 049628 issued by the Special Delegation at Yunnanfu.
Sokoloff was formerly a pilot in the Chinese Air Force.
They were both expelled from Burmese territory into Chinese
territory. Neither should be allowed to land in the Colony.
3./ALBINSKI, VICTOR. (Para. 4/34).
Native of Bosnia, Jugo-Slavia, aged 30 years, holder of
Polish Passport No. 32/30, Serial No. 161925, issued by the
Polish Legation, Shanghai, on 6th May, 1930, and valid till
1935.
This man left Shanghai at the end of August, 1933, with
the intention of making the journey to Poland overland by
bicycle. On reaching Changsha he was arrested by the Chinese
authorities who cancelled his Chinese visa on the grounds that
he had passed through prohibited, i.e., communist territory.
He was sent to Canton and after spending some weeks in prison
there, was sent to Hong Kong. The fact that the Chinese had
cancelled his visa obsessed him and his behaviour necessitated
his removal to hospital for observation. Meanwhile, the
Polish Minister in Shanghai, with whom he had communicated,

(3)
made representations to H.B.M. Consul-General, Shanghai, who
cabled saying that Albinski was an honest and harmless
individual but weak minded. An expulsion order was made
against Albinski who left Hong Kong by road on his bicycle
on 5th January, 1934, bound for Poland via China and Indo-
China. It is not suspected that this man is undesirable
politically but on account of his peculiar mentality is a
most difficult character to deal with. He should be made
the subject of a report in the event of his passing through
Malaya.
4. GEORGES ASSAISSO alias DON JUAN BAEZA alias MOULAY MUSTAFA
EL RAISUNI alias DR. M.E. RAISUNI. (Paras. 16, 28/35).
An international swindler with 20 convictions recorded
against him for fraud and larceny in Madrid, Paris, Denmark
and Northern Africa. His last conviction was at Copenhagen on
20th December, 1933, when he was sentenced to 10 months'
imprisonment for theft from a woman's flat. He poses as a
palmist and faith healer and commits theft from women whom
he visits when "faith healing". He is in possession of a
Spanish passport in the name of Don Juan Baeza issued in
London on 11th July, 1933. On 26th December, 1934, he arrived
in Bombay from Europe and posed as a brother-in-law of Amir
Abdul Kerim of Riff fame in an endeavour to obtain financial
assistance from leading Indian Mohammedan princes. He
journied to Calcutta where he got into trouble with the Police
over a brawl with a woman and was ordered to leave India. He
went to Colombo and sailed for Penang by the s.s. "Antenor"
on 14th April, 1935, en route for Manila. He passed through
Singapore on 5th May, 1935, and is now in Manila. He should
be refused permission to land in Malaya. His photograph
is filed in the Detective Branch, Singapore.
He has left Manila and is now in Shanghai.

Becker, described as a photographer and Hopner as a

7. BERGH, MRS. EMMI. (Paras. 1/34 & 5/34).

German Jewess, married to a Norwegian from whom she is
now divorced but retains Norwegian status. Arrived in
Singapore from Colombo on 2nd January, 1934, per the s.s.
"Le Conte De Lisle". She was practically destitute and
proceeded to reside at the "Lanka" Hotel, Trafalgar Street,
a Ceylonese boarding-house, and consorted for immoral
purposes with all nationalities. She was arrested on a
vagrancy charge but her board has been guaranteed in the
Y.W.C.A. until such time as arrangements are made to
repatriate her to Europe.

This woman was repatriated to France at Government
expense per the s.s. "D'Artagnan" on 5th February, 1934.
She should not be allowed to re-enter the Colony.

✓8. BOLKART, JOSEPH. (Para. 6/32).

A German subject. Arrested in Singapore on an ex-
tradition warrant applied for by the Consul-General for
the Netherlands. On 2nd September, 1932, was ordered to
be sent back to Java on charges of obtaining goods by false
pretences. He twice escaped from legal custody in Java
and should be noted for exclusion from the Colony should
he be released from Jail in Java.

No. † 9. BUMBA, WILLIAM. (Para. 18/34).

Aged 26 years, born at Ostrava, Czecho-Slovakia.

(5)
(C.I.D. 2/1670/34) This man arrived in Hong Kong as a
stowaway from Singapore in the s.s. "Lima Maru" on 17th
February, 1934. His story was that he boarded the s.s.
"Ouderkirk" at Port Said as a stowaway and that on being
discovered was put to work by the captain who agreed to
take him to Shanghai where he expected to find friends.
On arrival at Singapore on 7th February, 1934, the captain
of s.s. "Ouderkirk" found that he would have to call at
Manila, and telling Bumba that he could take him no further
as he feared trouble with the Manila Police, told him to
go ashore. The captain did not tell Singapore authorities
of his action, and Bumba came to Hong Kong as stated.
Bumba is at present in the House of Detention, Hong Kong,
and when the s.s. "Ouderkirk" calls in Hong Kong on or about
30th March, 1934 enquiries will be made regarding his story.
10. (1) BURTON, MISS PAULA. }
(2) HALEY, MISS ALBERTINA. } (Para. 47/34).

Curylo, accompanied by his wife, arrived in Singapore
by the s.s. "Haruna Maru" on 7th February, 1934, from Hong
Kong. He was in possession of a Polish passport issued in
Shanghai, and described himself as a merchant.

Komlenko, accompanied by his wife arrived in Singapore
by the same vessel and also from Hong Kong. He was in
possession of a Chinese passport issued in Shanghai and
described himself as a merchant.

Curylo and Komlenko, together with Ribiero (page 31 )
and V.A. Ogli (P.J. para. 73/33) had arrived together in
Hong Kong from Shanghai on 16th November, 1933. Ogli pro-
ceeded direct to Bangkok as he had previously been refused
permission to land in Malaya. The remainder came on to
Singapore as stated. In Shanghai Curylo was in partnership
with Komlenko in the "Black Eyes" Restaurant of 774, Avenue
Joffre, and of doubtful reputation. In Singapore they
stayed at the Adelphi Hotel, then moved to the Metropole
Hotel and are now staying at a Chinese Hotel in Beach Road.
Komlenko approached a well known local Chinese shortly after
his arrival and stated that he was in possession of a
secret process for manufacturing counterfeit currency notes
by chemical means. He wanted the Chinese to put up a sum
of $50,000 as capital and guaranteed that the money would
be doubled within a short space of time. It is quite appar-
ent that he was attempting a clever confidence trick and
the whole gang is extremely undesirable. Further enquiries

(8)
are being made regarding them.
Vladislav Peter Curylo and Vassili John Komlenko,
accompanied by their families, left Singapore by train for
Penang on 22nd April, 1934. Mrs. Ogli, wife of Ogli who
was convicted in Penang in 1933 for entering the Colony
without a valid passport, was also in their party. A dis-
creet report on their movements is requested.
Vladislav Peter Curylo, Vassili John Komlenko and
Lola Ogli arrived in Kuala Lumpur from Singapore on 1st
May, 1934, and proceeded to reside at the Yashmoya Hotel,
163, Batu Road. Nos. 2 and 3 left Kuala Lumpur on 2nd May,
1934, ostensibly for Seremban but did not arrive there. On
4th May, 1934, they returned to Kuala Lumpur and when
interviewed stated they had got out of the train near
Seremban and went off by a hired car to inspect rubber
estates with a view to purchase. They were unable to say
what estates were visited and their conduct appeared highly
suspicious. They then stated they were contemplating taking
over the Victoria Bakery, Kuala Lumpur, as a going concern.
This apparently fell through and they all left for Penang on
10th May, 1934. They are obviously a shady lot and require
careful surveillance.
The above named are now resident in Penang awaiting
permission to proceed to British India. A watch is being
kept on their movements but nothing suspicious has been noted
up to the present.
Curylo, P.V. and family left for Hong Kong by s.s.
"Katori Maru" on the 26th February, 1935.
Komlenko, V.J. left for Hong Kong by s.s. "Hong Peng"
on 7th February, 1935.

Kuhnle, a male German, born 1903 at Mannheim, an engineer

Hotel and later at 4, Eu Court registering as Mr. and Mrs.
Kuhnle. They became friendly with Ludwig Von Hornstein,

fire and it is suspected that this was an attempt to de-
fraud an insurance company as the launch had just been
insured for $4,300.

61. PRIOR, CHARLES LAWRENCE. (Paras. 43/34/& 25/35).

    In 1900 was gazetted to the 17th Lancers and left
this Regiment in 1906 on being transferred to the Reserve

(28)
of Officers. He was recalled to the Army in 1914 and re-
tired with the rank of Lt. Col. in 1919 but remained on the
Reserve of Officers. After the war he was for a time em-
ployed on a half commission basis with firms of stock
brokers in London and as Director of Companies dealing with
estates and buildings. He was of very extravagant habits
with the result that he was finally declared a bankrupt
after his people had repeatedly assisted him. He was adjud-
ged bankrupt on 7th May, 1925, with liabilities totalling
£9,769.10.0. and assets nil. He has not yet been discharged.
On 13th July, 1927, he was convicted before the Central
Criminal Court, London, on three charges of unlawfully
obtaining credit whilst an undischarged bankrupt. At the
same time he pleaded "not guilty" to four other indictments
charging him with fraudulent conversion of over £700.
The latter were not proceeded with and in the first
three charges he was bound over the Judge being influenced
by the fact that arrangements were made for the prisoner
to go abroad. He was also removed the Army List. He
arrived in Malaya about September, 1927, as agent for A.C.
Cars. In 1929 and 1930 he gave considerable trouble to the
authorities in Perak in connection with the Perak Transport
Company, of which he was manager. He arrived back in
Singapore in 1933 and promoted a livestock exhibition at
the "Great World". The show was a failure financially,
and money is still owed to various creditors. In 1934 he pro-
moted a Malayan Livestock Exhibition at the old Racecourse.
The exhibition commenced with very little capital, and
closed down on 23rd April, 1934, through lack of funds.
One of the creditors of the Exhibition took criminal
proceedings against Prior for cheating but the matter was
eventually settled. Numerous other similar complaints

(29)
were made and it is possible that further proceedings
will be taken.
Col. Prior is now preparing to go to Canton to act
as Secretary of a Greyhound Racing Association but final
arrangements have not yet been made. He has issued many
worthless cheques in Singapore and should be kept under
observation.
Prior's scheme for promoting Greyhound racing in
Canton failed owing to the refusal by the Chinese Govern-
ment to grant a license to the Company. He is now pro-
moting a company known as the Malayan Building Society
which has for its model the well known and powerful
Halifax Building Society of England. He is handicapped
by lack of capital and his affairs are being closely
watched. He has also advertised himself as a house and
land agent for which business he possesses no license.
He has been summoned for a breach of Ordinance No.95
(Auctioneers' Licenses) and the case will be heard in
August.
He was convicted on 5th August, 1935, before the Dis-
trict Judge, Singapore, for a breach of Ordinance No.95
(Auctioneers' Licenses). In view of his record the Colonial
Secretary has refused to issue to him a licence to act as
an house agent.

63. (1) RAUH, ALFRED (German). }
    (2) BAHR, HENRY (German).   } (Para. 30/35).

Rauh visited Singapore from Shanghai on 22nd April,
1932, described himself as a merchant and stayed at the
Hotel Metropole. He returned to Shanghai after 5 days in
Singapore. He again visited Singapore on 15th May, 1932,
and left on 26th June, 1933, for Hong Kong. He was in
possession of a passport No. 126/32 issued at Berlin on
1st April, 1932.

Bahr arrived on 22nd April, 1932, from Manila and also
described himself as a merchant and stayed at the Hotel
Metropole. He left for Bangkok on 6th May, 1933, returned
to Singapore on 16th May, 1933, and finally left for
Hong Kong on 6th July, 1933. He was in possession of a
passport No. 185, issued at Shanghai on 10th September,
1929. Whilst in Singapore in 1933, Rauh posed as a wealthy
man and Bahr as his secretary. They demonstrated to
credulous Asiatics what they termed a secret process for
manufacturing currency notes by means of chemicals from
genuine notes and attempted to obtain large quantities of gen-
uine notes for duplication. They failed and left for Hong
Kong as stated. They are a pair of international confidence
tricksters. Information has been received that Alfred Rauh's
real name is Albert Rosenbaum and is known to have been in
direct contact with a "drug ring" in China. He obtained
by trickery a Canadian passport No. 72546 granted on 22nd
February, 1934, at Montreal.

Their return to Malaya should be immediately reported
to the Detective Branch, where their photographs are filed.
The Canadian passport No. 72546 should be immediately
impounded if presented.

64. RIBIERO, RODRIGO ALVARA VIERA, alias ROBERTS alias RICHARDSON,
alias MAURICE RILEY. (Paras. 8, 15 & 24/34).

Portugese, born in Hong Kong, 1894. He is in possession
of a British passport issued in Hong Kong. He was sentenced
in Hong Kong on 19th October, 1914, to two years' R.I.
concurrently on each of three counts of forgery after having
been extradited from Colombo. He was released on 2nd
February, 1916, and proceeded to Macao where he was con-
victed of a similar offence and banished to Timor for six
years. He returned to Hong Kong and in 1926 was strongly
suspected of being party to a conspiracy which resulted in
the Netherlands Indische Handelsbank being defrauded of
$30,000 by a clever cheque fraud. He was employed in the
bank as a clerk at the time and left under mysterious
circumstances. Sufficient evidence was not obtained to
justify prosecuting him.

He arrived in Singapore from Hong Kong per the s.s.
"Conte de Rosso" on 14th February, 1934, accompanied by a
Chinese girl described as his wife although he is stated to
have a legal wife in Shanghai. In Singapore he is now
staying at the Central Hotel and claims to be the repre-
sentative of the "Hong Kong Pictorial" and is canvassing
for advertisements. He is an associate of the persons
referred to in page 7 and the fact that they all arrived
in Singapore from Hong Kong about the same time appears
suspicious and their movements should be made the subject
of discreet reports.

He disappeared from the Central Hotel, Singapore, on
or about 26th March, 1934, together with his Chinese mistress
and his present whereabouts unknown. Enquiries are requested
in an effort to locate him.

There is still no trace of his whereabouts.

REPO...

Subject Filipino Club at 258 Range Road.

Made by D.S. Kourjansky. Forwarded by N. Medvedeff, D.S.

I beg to report that on a recent visit of foreign lodging houses on Range Road, I noticed a "Room to let" signboard on the front wall of premises No. 258 Range Road.

The occupants did not apply for licence for operating the premises in question as a Foreign Lodging house, therefore, I interviewed the former when the following was ascertained:-

The above house has been rented on May 16, 1937 by a Filipino named Mr. Jesus Y. Iglesias, aged 32, on behalf of the Filipino Club known under the name of "Lipunang Filipino" of which he is the secretary.

The club is headed by a president named Mr. A.Y. Celis and consists of 42 members at present. According to the rules of the club, 85 % of the members must be of the Filipino nationality and the remainder, Chinese, Spanish, and Americans.

The club, it is stated, was organised for the purpose of social entertainments and it is understood, that "Mah Jong" and "Bridge" parties will be arranged for the members from time to time.

Mr. Iglesias stated that practically all the premises are occupied by the club with the exception of two attic rooms which they intend to let. According to Mr. Iglesias, application for permission for the club was recently submitted by them to the U.S.A. Consulate General.

I pointed out to Mr. Iglesias that since they have two rooms to let and that there is a possibility that in future they may change their mind and have a larger number of rooms to let, application to the S.M.C. on their part for licence for Foreign Lodging house would be necessary to which he replied that he will take the matter up with the committee.

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, THURSDAY, NOVEMBER 28, 1935

LEGAL DEFINITION OF
HOTEL SOUGHT

The word "hotel" should be pro-
perly defined and bona fide establish-
ments certificated by the Government.
said Sir Henry Kimber, chairman of
the Country Committee of the Hotels
and Restaurants Association, in a
speech at the Wine and Food Con-
ference at Bath.
He was anxious to see some
restriction put upon the word "hotel."
Many attempts had been made, with-
out success, to find a satisfactory de-
finition. Hotels, especially the small-
er ones, suffered a great deal from
the very unfair use of the word, and
some steps should be taken to stop
it.
An effective method could be found
by empowering a Government de-
partment to issue a certificate to
every establishment that could satisfy
it that it was a bona fide hotel, and
by making it illegal for anyone
without the certificate to call his
house a hotel.

Sir, I beg to forward the following as
the result of my investigations on the
attached enquiry.

Del Monte Cafe.
No gambling is known to be conducted on
the premises, although owing to the locality
of the cafe and to the large amount of
spare rooms in the upstairs portion of the
premises, there may be occasional nights
when private gambling is indulged in by
a few of the patrons. No immoral conduct
is conducted on the premises as the class
of "Dancing Partners" employed there is of
a type superior to those employed in
other cafes. Many of them however are
kept by foreigners of the wealthier class in
Shanghai, while not a few of them work
to keep their families. Mr. J. Hyde, an
american citizen has been manager of the
Del Monte for several years, and to appearance
the premises are well conducted. No other
foreigners are employed.

St. Georges Cafe.
This cafe was formerly owned by an
naturalized American citizen, named
Fredericks, who died about two years
ago, the business being handed over

to his kept women, who disposed of it to her
manager and paramour E. Bartels, a
German citizen. Bartels then carried on
the business and allowed it to develope
into a low class dancing saloon, which
was largely patronized by British and
American soldiers and sailors. Fight between
the members of the above nationalities was
a common occurrence and on several
occasions the premises were placed "Out of
Bounds" to British and American troops.
The dancing girls, employed in this cafe
at that time, were nearly all prostitutes,
and while no actual prostitution was ever
committed on the premises arrangements
were made by visitors to the cafe, whereby
they met the girls on their leaving the premises
and escorted them to their homes, chiefly in
Avenue Joffre, for the purpose of sexual
intercourse. It is not known that gambling
was ever permitted on the premises. Recently
the premises were disposed of to Jimmy James,
an American citizen and proprietor of the
several places in Shanghai, known as
Gimmy's Kitchen. Bartels was retained
by J. James, as his manager, and the
premises are now conducted in a greatly
improved manner, only Beer, cocktails
and light wines being sold on the
premises for consumption. There are

File No.
(C.I.D.) Office Notes
about 13 dancing girls at present employed,
mostly Japanese and Eurasian, and
the premises still continue to be patronized
by men of the British and American
army + navy units. No immoral conduct
is known to take place on the premises,
but it is possible that male visitors still
meet the dancing partners on leaving
the cafe and escort them to their homes
for the purpose of prostitution.
Welcome Cafe.
This cafe is owned by a former Chinese
boy named S. F. Chan, who is also
interested in the "Black Cat" cafe,
Thibet Road. It is not known that
gambling or immoral conduct is
permitted on the premises, nor is there
rooms available for this purpose. No
foreigners are employed and the premises
are patronized by foreigners and Chinese
alike, most of whom are visitors to
Jessfield Park in the afternoons. The
cafe is also well patronized in the
summer evenings by visitors touring
round the outlying roads of the Western
District. in motor cars. No dancing
partners are employed in this cafe.
Picnic Cafe.
This cafe adjoins the Welcome cafe

and was formerly owned by Messrs. Bianchi,
Nanking Road. It is owned by a chinese
named G. Y. Char, a former boy, and
the same remarks apply to it as apply
to the Welcome Cafe.
91 Seymour Road is occupied by
Dr. A. Bary, the well known Russian
brain specialist.

May 14, 1938.

Senior Detective i/o C.I.D.
Hongkew Station.

Please forward as soon as possible complete
list of cabarets, cafes and bars in your district,
giving names of proprietors, class of license issued,
number of dancing partners (if any) and nationality,
and a brief summary of the class of people who
frequent these establishments and any other details
of importance regarding these places. Further
reports will be forwarded as new premises open or
old ones close.

A. C. P. (Crime)

96 Broadway. Savoy Hotel. Patrons mixed, but mostly of the
sea-faring class. Two foreign assistant managers are employed
in the bar (one an American named J. Logan, the other a Britisher
named Billy Hodges) both have been in Shanghai for a number of
years, at one time were connected with the "Wheel", 24 North
Honan Road Extension. The dancing girls in the cabaret are
mostly Russians of the usual type, to be found in Shanghai
cabarets. The licensee A. Popovitch is also a long resident of
Shanghai and was connected with the old gambling resort "Alambra"
years ago. Occasionally foreigners of the undesirable type reside
at the hotel, who find it convenient for a short stay. The hotel,
cabaret and bar appears to be well controlled, no complaints are
ever received or made to the Police, neither have the Police had
occasion to interfere or warn the management. No comment.
86 Broadway. Eddie Cafe. Patrons are mixed, of all nationalities,
and occupation. The dancing girls are the usual type and nearly
all Russians. A British manager named E. Engley, formerly a
Sergeant in the S.M.P. is in charge of the restaurant. A Russian
in charge of the cabaret, and an American in charge of the bar.
There are frequent changes in the last two mentioned positions,
and it is difficult to form an opinion of them. The place is
well under control and no complaints are received. No comments.
Nos. 86 and 96 Broadway are the only places where dancing girls
are engaged the average number in each place is 10, but these are
increased or decreased according to business requirements and their
engagement is not permanent.
119 Range Road. Hotel Royal. A residential and family hotel of
good reputation. No comments.
2 Yuhang Road. St. Diago. A low class restaurant. The proprietor
has many convictions for white slave traffic, opium and arms
smuggling. Patrons are mostly sea-faring men and the place is also
frequented by women of loose morals. A license was given to the
proprietor, so that the police could have a better control over the
place. No complaints have been received since this place has been
licensed.

Detective opinion - A place which requires constant observation.
258 Boone Road patrons are mostly American Naval
men. Little business is done and the proprietor intends closing down.
31 Seward Road. Crystal Cafe. The proprietor is a noted arms smug-
gler and the place is often frequented by men who are known to the
police as dealer in arms, which includes also Chinese.
Detective opinion - A place which requires constant observation.
24 Haining Road. "Jocks Bar". The real proprietor and manager is a
Chinese, formerly employed as a boy in West Hongkew Station. It is
a small bar, attached to the Victoria Cinema. Patrons are mixed.
No comments.
1 - 3 Miller Road. "Franks Grill". Patrons are mixed and mostly
U.S.Naval men. The place is well under control. No comments.
23/4 N. Szechuen Road. Hongkew Hotel. This place is under Chinese
management, and patrons are chiefly Chinese, although occasionally
visited by foreigners. The place seems to be well controlled,
although at times the undesirable type of Chinese gains admission,
when usually gambling takes place, it is also visited by Chinese
females of loose morals, but if detected by the management, they are
quickly expelled, which at times requires police assistance.
Detective opinion - regular visits by detectives are required.
7/7a/8a Woochang Road. Linam Hotel. A Chinese hotel under Chinese
management, frequented mostly by Cantonese and occasionally by
foreigners accompanied by women of loose morals of all nationalities
Detective opinion - requires constant observation.
75 Broadway. A German restaurant, frequented by
foreigners of all nationalities. A place where good food and drinks
are served. No comments.
6a N. Soochow Road. Same as above (75 Broadway)
39 Seward Road. Same as 31 Seward Road. Needs constant
observation. Detective opinion - a doubtful place.
154 Range Road. A Russian restaurant, frequented by the Russian
Criminal classes. The proprietor is an ex-convict from Siberia,
and a license was given to this man, so that police could have a
better control over the place. Detective opinion - constant
observation required.

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
File No. 1249/6
C.S.6, Special Branch. /Sundry/ 111
REPORT
Date April 5, 1941.
Subject Reported Unlawful Activities in Foreign Lodging House No.2, Lane 1025,
(Hwa Kee Avenue), Bubbling Well Road.
Made by D.S. Mischenko. Forwarded by C.D.I. Tabrum.

I have to report that whilst inspecting
House No.2, Lane 1025, Bubbling Well Road, Mrs.C.I.
ZRITNEFF, the licensee of the house, informed me that
she suspects the occupant of Room No.2, a Korean,
registered under the name of Li Sz Ying, 30 years old,
merchant, of dealing in narcotics.
According to Mrs.C.I.Zritneff and her adult
son Mr.Victor Zritneff, the said Korean is visited daily
by a large number of Orientals - also suspicious looking
characters; the visitors using the front gate leading
directly into the room of the Korean tenant who is living
in the room together with his wife and two children and
employs one female Chinese servant.
It is reported that the said Korean although
unemployed appears to be quite prosperous at present.
The rent for the room is paid regularly and there is no
evidence to show that Mrs.C.I.Zritneff imparted the
information with a view to get rid of the tenant in
order to obtain a higher rent for the room.

D. Mischenko
D. S.

A.C.(Special Branch).
